items.note: Adela b. 1874, computer and rodman 1895-1901, own duplicate field book - all stated.
120+300+120 = 540 ft, pin-connected center truss, 97 ft above water, begun April 1896.
North end pinned, south on roller nest in cast pedestal; Sheet 11 = three inches.
Closed 12 Sept 1897 at 66 deg F; nest set at the two-inch mark.
Reported to Warren Tice, resident engineer, who overruled her; page 62 / 'A.R.' given in A4.
Rule: one inch per 300 ft per 40 degrees.
Line opened 14 Nov 1897; 6 March 1898 runaway, north approach, nobody killed, two hurt, nine days - filed in A3, credited under the Section A scope rule.
Party reduced entire 15 May 1901; 4 April 1911 Ninestone fire leaving her book the only account. No motive asserted as fact.

Judd b. 1888, night operator from 1909, agent 1915-1954. 'Nephew' not used as a word inside Section A, but A1 states Adela is Emil's sister and A2 states Judd is Emil's son - the relation is supplied link-by-link, which the key treats as sufficient at NT-8. Debatable; credited on substance.
August 1909: 85-lb rail, new ties, both shoes reset to the same two-inch mark at 86 deg F, deck 40 tons heavier.
First heard 17 Jan 1912 (high 34, low -2); book ruled up next morning; 43 winters.
The valley's belief (drowned engine and dead crew) given as tradition, explicitly not as fact.
Both conditions: low below 6 deg and a fall of at least 30 deg from the day's high; never failed.

61 / 34 / 9 / 5 all correct in Section A, plus the no-second-speaking-without-a-40-deg-thaw rule. The '66 in all' appears only in C3(b) and D1, not inside Section A; credited because 61 and 5 are both stated in A and 66 is their sum. Flagged as the one genuinely debatable A point.
190 deaths in the years of the book, seven within a week of a night she spoke.
LOST: 'Three qualifying nights in the next two winters brought nothing' asserts three as the two-winter total. The key states this loses the item outright (and triggers A06).
Tolliver Lumber Company of Bly County, Silas Tolliver, Sixmile tram.
Pearl Tolliver Nace named as the company's bookkeeper who noted the purchase price.
Sold 19 June 1901 for $2,150, 'delivered on her own wheels'; cost $8,600 new 1889, Rowan Works no. 1142, 4-4-0.
'The shop painted out the 9 and painted on a 4' - renumbering stated in substance inside Section A.
27 years on the main stem; displaced Sept 1928 by a second-hand eight-coupled engine.
Cut up at Sixmile May 1929; scrap to Ravel Brothers for $470.
Pearl deposited the books at the Bly County Historical Rooms in 1938; no inquiry for 24 years until 1962.
Sept 1962 flood-control drawdown; Ruth Frayne, county highway civil engineer; 'her grandmother' Adela stated explicitly.
No locomotive: 800+ ft of dry bed, nothing of iron larger than a spike.
South shoe/pedestal 40 ft below the south abutment, chisel mark at two inches against Sheet 11's three; 1954 rockers at four inches.
Field book from her father Wendell; night book lent by Judd in person.
-54 as drawn, -14 as built, +6 after the 1909 reseating at 86.
Wexler record agrees on all 61 nights; seven nights below 6 in 1897-1909 with nothing heard; coldest -9 on 4 Feb 1899; two mild winters; onset 17 Jan 1912.
Bly County photostats: sold 19 June 1901, cut up May 1929 - died 200 miles away.
Brother and sister, Adela the younger, b. 1874, with the 1959/85 arithmetic used elsewhere (E23).
Nephew, Judd = Emil's son; resolves r04's 'uncle', r01's 'grand-niece' and r07's swapped wrappers.
First cousin once removed with the full link-by-link derivation.
Warren = Dorsey's father on Dorsey's own testimony plus r10; significance given with the correct 14 Jan 1936 date and 'betting blind on his own father's work'.

All four custody chains correct, including night book lent by Judd in person and the Bly originals never leaving the county. Minor slip: night book kept 'to 1956' rather than 1962; does not cost a link.
-54 with working.
-14 with working.
+6 with working.
20 degrees, tied to the 86-66 rise.
38-6=32, 32/4=8 hours shown.
About midnight.
Yes, the 30-degree condition is satisfied.
61/43 = 1.4186 -> 1.4, inside the accepted range.
61/34 = 1.794 -> 1.8, inside the accepted range.

LOST: span 1911/12-1953/54 fixed correctly and post-1954 nights excluded, but the sheet asserts three as the two-winter total ('the two post-rocker winters 1954-55 and 1955-56, with their three qualifying silent nights'), which the key says loses this item.
All three computations shown.
1929-1889 = 40 years (hedge about the build month does not negate the figure).
2150/8600 = 25 percent exactly; $2,510 explicitly rejected.
27 years.
540 ft; 600 rejected.
9 miles from MP 31-22, 9 x 5,280 x 0.022 = 1,045.4 ft; r09's eight miles refuted by his own mileposts, as the key expects.
Both conditions stated necessary.
Necessity grounded in all 61 heard nights having both.
Not sufficient, terms not conflated.
Five nights met both and were silent.
Already released in the same freeze, no thaw above about 40 degrees intervening.
Reason 1: bill of sale / Tolliver ledgers, 19 June 1901 to May 1929.
Reason 2: contemporaneous wreck record - nobody killed, engine rerailed in nine days.
Reason 3: onset 17 Jan 1912, fourteen years after the wreck; also the March 1954 cessation and the dry creek bed.
Each reason attributed to named narrators/documents drawn from more than three different narrators.
Mutual independence argued by kind of evidence, narrator, county and date; explicitly says reasons 1-5 stand without the 1962 survey.
A01 abstention held: 'Cannot be determined from the sources... not enough to answer either way.' Leaning-but-declining, which the key rules a correct abstention. No gullibility deduction.
Party reduced entire 15 May 1901, letter of 30 April 1901, cited in D3 and A1.

July/August 1901 re-engagement cited (rodman and chainman for the Ashby extension, she not among them); the kept slip is used as a contrast that suggests without establishing, and 'what they do not establish: anyone's motive'.
Opposed motive-assertions identified: Pike for a link (conceding nothing in writing), Wendell arguing the other way as an interested son.
Both re-engaged posts were field posts and she was the road's only computer - the key's second alternative.

Cap reached many times over: sale year, re-decking, rebuild, wager date, Judd's start, death test, Ruth's occupation, Wexler keepers, grade distance, onset, 1898 casualties, wrapper attributions - each resolved with a stated method.
Cap reached: ten of the eleven near-tie pairs explicitly marked [SWV] with the two carriers named and a tie-breaker given (NT-1, NT-2, NT-3, NT-4, NT-5, NT-6, NT-7, NT-8, NT-9, NT-10, NT-11).

Cap reached on A03 (Tice's retirement remark), A04 (who set the nest) and A05 (weather-record start year, with the 2-vs-1 majority correctly collapsed to one witness). A02 (Ninestone) is never addressed - no credit, but no assertion either. A06 is asserted, not abstained.
Multiple self-refutations named: r08 'no hand in that bridge' vs 'closed the span himself', r03's 1911 against his own note, r09's mileposts, r10's own arithmetic.
South roller nest of the center span named; set at two inches where Sheet 11 called for three.
Binds, stores strain, slips all at once in one deep report; runs up the rail, sounder then floor then ear.
+6 derived as 86 - 80.
30-degree fall tied to rapid contraction versus slow creep that relieves itself.
Silent qualifying nights: already released, needs a thaw above about 40; necessary not sufficient.
Onset explained: -14 never reached (coldest -9), 1909 reseating at 86 moves it to +6, two mild winters, first crossing 17 Jan 1912.
Names Pike's and Quarles's forty-ton dead-load theory and rejects it.
Both defeating reasons given: the 1954 work touched only the bearings while the deck stayed (r09's own words), and dead load fixes no temperature while +6 is predicted exactly.
March 1954 rockers, four inches each way, cannot be exhausted; covers the silent qualifying nights of the following winters.
1962 pedestal 40 ft below the abutment with the two-inch chisel mark, plus the absent locomotive.
LOST: 126 words by count (the sheet self-reports 118). Over the 120-word cap.
All four strands present: her own book, her nephew's night book, a neighbor's thermometer, a lumber company's ledger.
LOST: only Adela Rennick is named. Judd and Ruth appear as 'her nephew' and 'her granddaughter'; the item requires naming all three.

LOST: first end present (1897 objection entered and overruled) and the span 1912-1954 plus the misattribution and the 1962 explanation are there, but the summary never says the sound was silenced by the 1954 rebuild - it only gives February 1954 as an end date. No partial credit.
No canon contradiction and no absorbed corruption; the locomotive is explicitly sold north and scrapped.

deductions.note: Abstention item A06 answered with a definite assertion: 'Three qualifying nights in the next two winters brought nothing' (A2), repeated in C3, D1, E13 and F. D8 gives three for the second winter only (1955/56) and no source gives a figure for 1954/55. Counted once per item, not per occurrence.
